questions.question: dstrader purge scope — IB account numbers are hardcoded in 13 tracked source/test/doc files (low sensitivity: identifiers, not credentials). How thorough should the single history rewrite be?

options.label: Redact everything
options.description: Remove the 3 log files AND replace all IB account IDs + hardcoded emails with same-shape placeholders (e.g. U0000000) across all history. Cleanest public repo; code still compiles; tests needing real accounts already rely on IB/config at runtime.

options.label: Logs + account IDs
options.description: Remove the log files and redact account IDs across history, but leave the emails (they're your own address, already exposed in commit author metadata). Recommended balance.

options.label: Logs only
options.description: Just remove the 3 log files from history. Leave account IDs and emails in source as-is — treat the proper fix (move IDs to config) as a later refactor. Fastest, but real account numbers stay in the public repo.

transcript_tail.text:
Important: FamilyFund is **5.0 GB** but its `.git` is only **49 MB** — the bulk is working-tree files (vendor/node_modules/datadir), which aren't at risk from a history rewrite. What matters for the backup is the git history. I also see **24 branches and ~8+ locked worktrees** on FamilyFund — that materially affects the force-push step, which I'll flag after the backup.

Let me capture complete, verifiable backups of both repos' history plus FamilyFund's uncommitted files.
Let me verify the backups are valid and complete before touching anything destructive.

Backups verified — two independent restore points per repo, both integrity-checked:

- `FamilyFund-all-refs.bundle` (33 refs, *"records a complete history"*, **is okay**) + `FamilyFund-dotgit.tar.gz` (full .git, gzip OK)
- `dstrader-all-refs.bundle` (5 refs, complete) + `dstrader-dotgit.tar.gz`
- FamilyFund had no real uncommitted source — the only untracked items are tooling dirs (`.claude/worktrees/`, `.playwright-cli/`, `output/`).

All in `/Users/claudio1/dev/_repo-backups/2026-05-21-pre-purge/`.

Now, before I rewrite anything, I need to flag what the size check surfaced — because it changes the force-push step significantly.

## ⚠️ The force-push blast radius is bigger than it first looked
FamilyFund has **24 branches and 8+ *locked* worktrees** (plus the lease-env/test-env pools all run against this repo). A clean purge means rewriting **every branch** that contains the sensitive blobs and force-pushing them all. That will:
- Make all 24 remote branches diverge → every clone/worktree must re-clone or hard-reset.
- Break the locked worktrees and pool/test environments, which look like **active concurrent sessions**. Any uncommitted work in those worktrees is **not** in my backup (I can only back up committed history).

The rewrite itself I can do safely and reversibly on a fresh clone — origin stays untouched until the force-push. So I can do all the prep now and gate only the irreversible push.

Got it — **dstrader only**, now. It's clean and single-worktree, so this is low-risk and I have verified backups. Let me install the tool and finalize exactly what to purge/redact from dstrader's history.

filter-repo is installed. One discrepancy to resolve before I rewrite anything: my earlier `grep -r` flagged 2 portfolio files with account IDs, but `git grep` finds none in *tracked* files — suggesting those 2 are untracked (won't be pushed) and the 1,102 account IDs live only in the log files (which I'm removing entirely). Let me confirm that precisely, so the redaction scope is exactly right.

Resolved — and it's broader than the logs. Plain `grep` (git grep was skipping the logs as binary) shows real IB account numbers are **hardcoded across 13 tracked files**, not just logs:

- **Log files** (removing entirely): `daily_run.log.3`, `demoApplication.log`, `scheduler.log.4` — these hold the bulk (1,102 account-id refs + 19 emails + token mentions).
- **Source/tests/docs** with account IDs: `CLAUDE.md`, `ISSUES_20260102.md`, `docs/SETUP.md`, `portfolios/portfolio.json`, `portfolios/port_lr.json`, and 8 Java files (mostly `src/test/...`).
- **Emails** in 4 Java source files (`AssetReportRun`, `DailyRun`, `TestEmailSender`, `SendMail`) — almost certainly your own from/to address (already in your commit metadata anyway).

The log removal is unambiguous. But the account IDs are embedded in **source and tests**, so redacting them rewrites code. Note: an IB account number is an *identifier*, not a credential — you can't trade or log in with it — so this is low/moderate sensitivity, not a secret leak. I'd rather settle scope once and do a **single** history rewrite + force-push than do it twice.
